hero.headline: The World Cup's best experiences happened outside the stadiums
hero.sub: Spain took the trophy at MetLife on July 19. Producers should study everything around it: fan festivals at two-million scale, a drone scoreboard over Seattle, and ticketed dome watch parties.
hero.statement: The best of the World Cup happened outside the stadiums.

sections.headline: The activations that worked gave fans a job to do
sections.body: Michelob ULTRA ran a two-week Pitchside Club on Santa Monica Pier with a 2,500-drone show; adidas built free Home of Soccer hubs across five cities with 3v3 tournaments. The pattern across Event Marketer's roundup: watching was table stakes. The activations people queued for handed them a ball, a game, a role.
sections.statement: The activations people remembered didn't ask to be watched.

sections.headline: The scoreboard in the sky was really a data pipeline
sections.body: Visit Seattle flew a 400-drone scoreboard beside the Space Needle after each hosted match: 12-minute shows rendering the score, flags and city imagery, billed as a first. The steal: any same-day feed — scores, votes, sales — can become sky-scale scenography.
sections.statement: A scoreboard in the sky is just a data pipeline with an audience.
sections.why: Any same-day feed can become sky-scale scenography.

sections.headline: The watch party is now a venue-grade product
sections.body: Fox Sports and FIFA put roughly 40 matches, the final included, inside Cosm's 87-foot 12K domes in LA, Dallas and Atlanta — with stadium cameras framed for the dome, not TV. The craft lesson: capture designed for the canvas beats repurposed broadcast.
sections.statement: The watch party grew up — it's a venue-grade product now.
sections.why: Capture built for the canvas beats repurposed broadcast.

video.headline: One minute, three stolen ideas
video.body: Sixty seconds through the tournament's off-pitch tech: a drone scoreboard over Seattle, shared-reality domes in three cities, and fan festivals two million strong. Watch with your next pitch open.

invitation.headline: Have something impossible in mind?
invitation.body: If the tournament left you with a brief that sounds unbuildable — a dome, a live-data show, a room that reacts — that is our favorite kind.
